transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-05-08 14:00 UTC
Duration: 47 minutes (approx)
Attendees: Liam Ortiz (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Nora Kim (Redwood Solutions), Marcus Lee (Solace Head of MLOps), Anika Patel (CTO), Diego Ramos (Security Engineer), Sara Nguyen (Cloud Eng)

Summary (auto): quick POC scoping for private networking and data residency. Focus areas: VPC peering vs PrivateLink, regions (EU/US), egress constraints (no internet egress), KMS and audit logs, workload sizing and benchmark plan, timeline ~4 weeks.

Transcript:
[00:00] Liam Ortiz: hey everyone thanks for joining, can you hear me ok?
[00:04] Marcus Lee: yeah can hear you, thanks. busy week but we wanted to lock down networking and residency up front.
[00:10] Priya Shah: cool, high level we'll scope a 4-week POC. first week network & security setup, second week baseline benchmarks, third week workload scale, fourth week ops/rollout decisions. that's flexible.
[00:25] Anika Patel: sounds good. our main blockers: data can't leave eu-west-1, no public internet egress from our VPC for inference, and we need KMS integration for key management.
[00:36] Priya Shah: understood, eu-west-1 only, KMS and audit logs. two common ways we connect: VPC peering/Privatelink via AWS PrivateLink; peering is simpler for persistent connections but PrivateLink gives more control and no cross-account routing complexity.
[00:52] Diego Ramos: quick question, Any egress to third-party monitoring or metric endpoints okay? we try to avoid any external egress.
[00:59] Priya Shah: so we can keep all inference traffic within region. metrics can optionally be forwarded to your monitoring via VPC endpoints; otherwise we can store logs in S3 inside the VPC (or with an S3 gateway endpoint) and you pull them.
[01:15] Sara Nguyen: do you support AWS PrivateLink in eu-west-1 today?
[01:18] Liam Ortiz: yes, Redwood Private supports PrivateLink and VPC peering. there are small differences: PrivateLink requires customers to accept the endpoint service and we provide the endpoint service in the region; peering requires route updates on both sides.
[01:31] Marcus Lee: ok, which one is recommended for a POC?
[01:34] Priya Shah: for short POCs we often recommend PrivateLink because it avoids full peering changes, and you can control NACLs/security groups strictly. but if you already have peering infra it's fine. note: if you use our Dedicated nodes in the same account we can avoid cross-account by deploying into your account - but that's a longer onboarding.
[01:53] Anika Patel: we prefer not to give an account role or host any redwood nodes in our account for the POC. PrivateLink + interface endpoints seems better.
[01:59] Priya Shah: great. on egress: we will not require any outbound internet to serve requests if you use PrivateLink and the model cache is region-local. there are some cases (model downloads, occasional telemetry) which we can turn off or route through your egress.
[02:17] Diego Ramos: we need to confirm KMS. we use customer-managed CMKs with key rotation and HSM-backed keys.
[02:23] Priya Shah: we integrate with KMS for data-at-rest encryption; for Redwood Private deployments we can support bringing your own KMS keys via cross-account grants. we'll send the exact IAM and grant steps.
[02:34] Liam Ortiz: let's move on to workload sizing - Marcus, can you share expected traffic patterns?
[02:38] Marcus Lee: sure. we're building a clinician-assist feature. average payload ~600 tokens in, 900 tokens out, peak 40 concurrent sessions during clinic hours (1pm-5pm CET), sustained 10 qps average across the day. monthly: about 15 million tokens.
[02:55] Priya Shah: ok so rough peak concurrency 40, target P95 latency under 250ms for short prompts, but for long chains we expect up to 500-800ms. is 250ms realistic as success criteria?
[03:10] Anika Patel: yes for quick lookups we want <300ms P95. for full generation flows we accept up to 800ms as long as throughput holds.
[03:18] Priya Shah: good. recommended POC config: a small Dedicated pool (2-3 GPUs) or Redwood Private in VPC with batching enabled, quantized model variant for cost. we'll propose a benchmark plan: synthetic rps test matching your token distribution, then replay a sample of real traffic if you can provide sanitized logs.
[03:37] Marcus Lee: we can share anonymized traces - will need NDA?
[03:40] Liam Ortiz: we have standard POC NDA and security addendum; we'll attach. for benchmarks, two goals: 1) latency SLOs (P50/P95/P99) and 2) cost per 1k tokens.
[03:52] Diego Ramos: also we need audit logs for each request, and per-token billing details for reconciliation.
[03:57] Priya Shah: audit logs are supported; we can stream them to your S3 with KMS encryption or to your SIEM over private connection. billing detail we can provide token-level usage CSVs for the POC.
[04:08] Sara Nguyen: how do we handle model variants / fallbacks if capacity is limited?
[04:12] Priya Shah: Redwood has smart routing - during the POC we can configure fallback to a slightly smaller model to preserve latency. we can also test degradation scenarios in the runbook.
[04:22] Anika Patel: what about regional restrictions - if we want only eu-west-1, can Redwood guarantee no egress to US?
[04:28] Liam Ortiz: yes, for PrivateLink in eu-west-1 we can ensure all inference runtime and model artifacts stay in-region. some telemetry backends are global by default but for enterprise/private we route telemetry to your endpoints or disable it. we'll document defaults in the security pack.
[04:42] Marcus Lee: timeline then - we need internal signoff by 2026-05-14 to start setup week of 2026-05-18. is that feasible?
[04:48] Priya Shah: yes. typical POC timeline: network setup + security review (1 week), baseline benchmark (1 week), scale and edge cases (1 week), review + handoff (1 week). so 4 weeks total.
[04:59] Diego Ramos: we'll need Redwood to provide the exact list of firewall rules and service IPs we need to whitelist.
[05:04] Priya Shah: absolutely, I'll include a CIDR list, endpoint service names, and example SG/NACL rules in the network checklist.
[05:12] Liam Ortiz: on sizing/cost - for your token volume we can propose two options: hosted with PrivateLink (pay-per-use, slightly higher per-token due to PrivateLink egress) vs small Dedicated pool (monthly commit, lower per-token on heavy usage). I'll follow up with numbers.
[05:26] Anika Patel: we'd like to see a simple TCO comparison for our expected monthly usage.
[05:30] Liam Ortiz: yes, we'll include TCO + latency tradeoffs.
[05:33] Marcus Lee: test plan - can you outline benchmarks you'll run?
[05:36] Priya Shah: yes, baseline single-user latency with your payload distribution; multi-client concurrency ramp to 60; cold-cache model download time; cache-warm perf; and a failover test to smaller model. we run both synthetic and replayed traffic. we'll capture P50/P95/P99 and cost metrics.
[05:51] Diego Ramos: also add security test for KMS key access and audit log integrity.
[05:55] Priya Shah: noted.
[05:57] Sara Nguyen: minor: how do we do DNS for PrivateLink endpoints. do you expose an internal hostname?
[06:02] Priya Shah: we supply the endpoint network interface. you can create private hosted zone entries for the endpoint DNS names; we'll include config examples.
[06:10] Marcus Lee: ok, any blockers from Redwood side?
[06:12] Nora Kim: we just need the CIDRs, KMS key ARN, and a point of contact for network acceptance. also permission to run a few synthetic load tests from Redwood test accounts into the endpoint during the POC window.
[06:25] Marcus Lee: fine, will share.
[06:28] Liam Ortiz: recapping next steps: Redwood to send network + PrivateLink checklist, security pack (SOC2, KMS steps, certs), pricing/TCO for Dedicated vs PrivateLink, and NDA/POC agreement. Solace to provide region confirmation, CIDRs, anonymized traces, and a POC PO if required.
[06:45] Anika Patel: we'll try to get signoff this week.
[06:48] Liam Ortiz: great. we'll target kickoff 2026-05-18. thanks everyone.
[06:51] Marcus Lee: thanks all.

Notes on transcript quality: occasional speaker overlap, some product names mis-transcribed (PrivateLink sometimes rendered as Private Link, KV cache as K V cash), minor filler words removed.
